answer.rationale: Current facts eliminate most directions before memory even applies: the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so memory_c4 (renegotiation recovered margin) is not actionable this cycle; renewal on existing terms (memory_c1, memory_c6) cannot deliver an 18% cut; and deferral (memory_c5) is unavailable because the contract does not auto-renew and there is no month-to-month fallback at 94% committed volume with no buffer. That leaves the low-cost vendor path, which rests almost entirely on memory_c2 — the single load-bearing memory here, and the weakest-specified one. It says cost fell 'sharply last year' with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, but it does not record whether that was this component, at this volume, under a no-buffer line, or whether on-time delivery performance (not invoicing accuracy) was ever measured. Invoicing accuracy is a billing signal being read as a fulfillment signal. So memory_c2 is the first verification pull: I need the original record's scope, volume, and delivery data before letting it carry a full primary switch. Second pull is memory_c3, because dual-sourcing 'held up through the shortage' is the only inherited evidence about behavior under supply stress, and it may show a cheaper way to buy delivery insurance while the new vendor qualifies. Intent is to move primary supply to the low-cost vendor but at guarded scale: qualify with a partial volume tranche and a bridge on the incumbent rather than cutting over the whole line inside 14 days. A 94% utilization line with zero buffer means a delivery miss is not recoverable, and the primary objective explicitly forbids buying cost savings with delivery risk. Downstream risk flagged: the 18% mandate creates pressure to treat memory_c2 as stronger than it is, and if I commit broadly on it and it is wrong, future sessions inherit 'the switch worked' or 'the switch failed' as a fact without ever recovering the volume and delivery caveats that were missing from the start. A guarded tranche also generates the delivery data this memory set never had. If verification shows memory_c2 came from a low-volume or non-critical component, I fall back to add_second_source and take a partial cut this cycle rather than the full mandate.
